claims.text: The Victoria Embankment Gardens are a beautiful series of green spaces situated on the north side of the River Thames.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: They were created on land that was newly reclaimed from the river when Sir Joseph Bazalgette built the northern embankment and sewer between 1865 and 1870.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The gardens were officially laid out in 1874, sitting on the inward side of the new roadway named the Victoria Embankment.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Originally, the project was split into four distinct sections, including the Temple Garden to the east and the Main Gardens, originally known as the Adelphi Gardens, to the west.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The two remaining sections were cleverly designed to the south to perfectly follow the natural bend of the River Thames.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, these historic and relaxing riverside spaces are maintained under the control of the City of Westminster.
claims.subject: self
